cheatSheet.oneLiner: Newton’s laws, friction, circular motion dynamics — forces cause acceleration.
mustKnowBullets: First law: inertia; net force zero ⇒ constant velocity.
Second law: F_net = dp/dt; for const mass, F = ma.
Third law: action–reaction pairs act on different bodies.
Momentum p = mv; impulse = Δp = F_avg Δt.
Friction: f_s ≤ μ_s N; f_k = μ_k N; opposes relative tendency/motion.
Banking / skidding: on level road v_max = √(μrg); banked WITHOUT friction v₀=√(Rg tanθ); banked WITH friction v_max=√[Rg(μs+tanθ)/(1−μs tanθ)].
Angle of repose: the maximum incline angle θ_max at which a block just remains on the verge of sliding satisfies tanθ_max = μs — numerically equal to the angle of friction.
Spring (restoring) force: F = −kx, where k is the force constant; negative sign shows the force opposes the displacement from the natural length.
Law of conservation of momentum: in an isolated system (no external force), total momentum before = total momentum after — a direct consequence of Newton's second and third laws together.
Connected bodies: common acceleration; tension from free-body diagrams.

highlights.text: Tendency of a body to resist change in its state of motion.
First law: inertia; net force zero ⇒ constant velocity.
Second law: F_net = dp/dt; for const mass, F = ma.
Third law: action–reaction pairs act on different bodies.
Apply sign convention and assumptions before substituting.
Newton’s laws, friction, circular motion dynamics — forces cause acceleration.

The total momentum of an isolated system of interacting particles is conserved: pA + pB = p'A + p'B, a direct consequence of Newton's second and third laws applied to a collision (F_AB Δt = p'A−pA and F_BA Δt = p'B−pB, with F_AB=−F_BA).
highlights.whyItMatters: The Law of Conservation of Momentum — a distinct named law, foundational for the collisions chapter, but its own testable statement here.

highlights.text: The spring (restoring) force is F = −kx, where k is the spring's force constant and x is the displacement from its natural (unstretched) length.
highlights.whyItMatters: Reused constantly in later chapters (oscillations, elastic PE) — the force law that defines SHM.

highlights.text: Angle of repose: as the incline of a plane is increased, a resting block begins to slide exactly when tanθ_max = μs (the coefficient of static friction). This maximum angle is independent of the mass of the block.
highlights.whyItMatters: One of the most frequently tested static-friction results — numerically identical to the 'angle of friction'.

highlights.text: For a car on a banked road WITH friction, the maximum safe speed is v_max = √[Rg(μs+tanθ)/(1−μs tanθ)], and the optimum speed (needing zero friction) is v₀=√(Rg tanθ).
highlights.whyItMatters: The general banked-curve formula — distinct from and more complete than the simpler frictionless-banking or flat-road-with-friction special cases.

In an isolated system with no external force, the total momentum before an interaction equals the total momentum after — a direct consequence of Newton's second and third laws.
The maximum angle of incline at which a block resting on it is on the verge of sliding; tanθ_max = μs, independent of the block's mass.
The restoring force exerted by a stretched or compressed spring, F=−kx, where k (the force constant) characterises the spring's stiffness.

formulas.name: Conservation of momentum
formulas.latex: p_A + p_B = p'_A + p'_B \quad \text{(no external force)}
formulas.plain: total momentum before an interaction = total momentum after, for an isolated system

symbols.meaning: initial momenta of the two bodies

formulas.whenToUse: Collisions, explosions, recoil (gun-bullet) problems — any isolated system with no net external force.
commonMistakes: Forgetting momentum is a VECTOR — components must be conserved separately along each axis, not just magnitudes.
Applying this when an external force (like friction from the ground) actually acts on the system during the interaction.

questionPatterns.patternName: Recoil of a gun firing a bullet
questionPatterns.howToInterpret: System starts at rest (zero total momentum); after firing, bullet and gun momenta must be equal and opposite.
questionPatterns.exampleStem: A gun of mass 3 kg fires a 0.03 kg bullet at 500 m/s. Find the recoil speed of the gun.

formulas.audioScript: This is really just Newton's third law dressed up in momentum language — since the two interacting bodies always push back on each other with equal and opposite force for the same time, their momentum changes must exactly cancel, leaving the total unchanged.

formulas.name: Banked road with friction (general case)
formulas.plain: maximum safe speed on a banked, frictional curve

symbols.meaning: coefficient of static friction between tyres and road

formulas.whenToUse: A banked curve where friction ALSO contributes to the centripetal force (the general, most realistic case) — reduces to v₀=√(Rg tanθ) when μs=0.
commonMistakes: Using the simpler frictionless-banking formula when the problem explicitly gives a coefficient of friction — that formula only gives the single 'optimum' speed, not the full safe range.

questionPatterns.patternName: Maximum speed on a banked, frictional racetrack
questionPatterns.howToInterpret: Identify R, θ, and μs; substitute directly.
questionPatterns.exampleStem: A racetrack of radius 300 m is banked at 15°. If μs between tyres and road is 0.2, find the maximum permissible speed to avoid slipping.

formulas.audioScript: This is the fully general banked-curve formula — friction and banking work together, so it correctly reduces to the simple frictionless case when there's no friction at all, and to the flat-road case when the banking angle is zero.
